triageGrades.reason: The diff rewrites the password-reset storage and lookup in backend/src/routes/auth.js, squarely an authentication flow, and the cited line is accurate.

The entire change is about how a credential — the reset token, the whole account-takeover secret — is persisted and compared (plaintext → SHA-256 digest via a new resetToken service), so secret/credential handling is plainly touched.
Nothing in the diff touches billing, Stripe, pricing, or quota accounting.
No deletions, drops, or bulk writes; the only data effect is the pre-existing per-user unset of the consumed token and refreshTokens clearing, unchanged by this diff.
The sendEmailRaw call site is untouched (only the token value it embeds comes from the same crypto.randomBytes), and the test stubs the mailer rather than adding any outbound call.
No deploy config, migration, env var, or version artifact changes — the stale-token invalidation is a PR-body note, not a release-surface change.

summary: A clean sheet was the right call here — the change is correct, complete (write site, read site, null-guard, and both halves behind one pure function), and the test's known digest and harness shape check out — but the local triage wrongly marked secrets as untouched when storing a credential safely is the whole point of the item.
